name: Maize Rust (Common Rust)
description: A fungal disease producing reddish-brown pustules on maize leaves. Common rust is favored by moderate temperatures while southern rust prefers warmer conditions. Both can cause significant yield loss when infections are severe.
symptoms: Small reddish-brown pustules on both leaf surfaces
Pustules rupturing to release powdery rust spores
Leaves turning yellow and dying prematurely
Reduced grain fill due to lost photosynthetic leaf area
causes: Puccinia sorghi (common rust) or Puccinia polysora (southern rust)
treatments: Apply fungicides containing azoxystrobin or pyraclostrobin
Spray tebuconazole or propiconazole at first signs
Use mancozeb as a protectant fungicide
Apply sulfur-based fungicides for mild infections
prevention: Ensure adequate plant spacing for air circulation
Monitor fields regularly during favorable weather
